div.head: VI Atr Lat 34
div.ab: Qua igitur etiam pena digni sint, qui nauium detrimentum in aliquibus perficiunt, notum cunctis esse cupimus. Quicunque aliquam ex nauibus per quampiam inertiam uel per incuriam uel neglegentiam corruperit, et tamen recuperabilis sit, is nauis corruptolam uel fracturam eiusdem persolidam prius recuperet, regique deinde ea, que pro eiusdem munitionis fractura sibimet pertinent, rite persoluat.
div.note: Latin paraphrase of VI Atr (early 11th c.; K = Cotton Claudius A III f. 30, perhaps by Archbishop Wulfstan), text in column K (Liebermann’s text; until October 2026 in column T). Liebermann gives no German translation for it: for the meaning see the matching Old English chapter of VI Atr above, which it paraphrases (Liebermann prints in small type the words that correspond exactly to the Old English).; T: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Liebermann’s Latin Paraphrase)”, now “∅ (moved to K)”)

note.seg: munitio (s. Ducange, auch munimen, -itas): ‘Verteidigung, Schutz(brief)’ soll mund übersetzen
munitio (see Ducange, also munimen, -itas): ‘defence, protection (or letter of protection)’ is meant to translate mund

Mit Unrecht verbindet Price-Thorpe hwa folces ‘jemand im Volke’; denn der Gen. part. pflegt voranzugehen; s. Toller s. v. hwa. Und folc (s. d. Wb 2) heisst in Kompositen öfter: ‘Staat, Nation’; s. Toller folcgestreon

Price-Thorpe wrongly takes hwa folces together as ‘someone among the people’; for the partitive genitive usually precedes; see Toller s. v. hwa. And folc (see that word in Wb 2) often means ‘state, nation’ in compounds; see Toller folcgestreon
‘bessere aus’, wie L vielleicht versteht, liesse ein Verb für munde vermissen (doch wäre Ellipse möglich) und gäbe nicht den Ggs. zu ‘entgelte voll’ nächsten Gedankens
‘make amends’, as L perhaps understands it, would leave munde without a verb (though an ellipsis would be possible) and would not provide the contrast with ‘pay in full’ in the next clause

Königs Gefolge und -Dienst, aber auch das Heer als solches, steht unter besonderem Schutz (s. d. Gl 9. c II. III). Hier ist Königsschutz (s. d. Gl 5. 8) = 5 £ gemeint. Diese Strafsumme kommt für Verletzung des Friedens oder der Folgepflicht im Heere (s. d. Gl 8ff.) sonst nicht vor

The king’s retinue and service, but also the army as such, are under special protection (see that word in Gl 9. c II. III). What is meant here is the king’s protection (see that word in Gl 5. 8) = 5 £. This penalty does not occur elsewhere for breach of the peace or of the duty of service in the army (see that word in Gl 8ff.)
